NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The proposed intervention is to apply a pulsed electrostatic discharge mitigation scheme during shock events to prevent stiction in MEMS capacitive accelerometer comb structures. Standard practice relies solely on mechanical design and spacing to prevent contact; our mitigation introduces a controlled electrostatic repulsion pulse that counteracts adhesive forces upon shock detection, directly addressing the van der Waals and capillary forces driving stiction. The closest existing technique is electrostatic self-testing in MEMS, which uses DC bias for diagnostics; our departure is the use of transient high-voltage pulses (not DC) for active stiction prevention during shock events, leveraging the same electrodes but with a new operational mode.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation for electrostatic force between parallel plates is F = ε₀AV²/(2d²), where ε₀ is permittivity, A is contact area, V is voltage, and d is gap. For a 100V pulse across a 1μm gap with 100μm² contact area, F ≈ 4.4×10⁻⁵N, sufficient to overcome typical stiction forces (10⁻⁷–10⁻⁶N range). This force acts normal to the contact plane, directly counteracting adhesion.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL (vs. standard practice):
- Standard practice: comb finger gap design, power supply, microcontroller, optical lever system
- Proposed intervention:
  - (a) Power supply (existing, repurposed for pulse generation)
  - (b) High-voltage pulse generator module (procurable standard catalog item, e.g., EMCO AG Series)
  - (c) Shock detection algorithm (parameter change to existing microcontroller code)
  - (c) Electrostatic pulse timing procedure (configuration change to existing electrodes)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY):
- Power supply: existing (a) — no change
- Microcontroller: existing (a) — software update only
- Optical lever system: existing (a) — no change
- HV pulse generator: new (b) — same class as existing power supply, comparable cost/size
- Total burden: same class as standard practice (minimal new hardware, software changes)

EXECUTABLE TEST:
- Protocol: Subject 10 devices to 10000g shock (per MIL-STD-883 Method 2002.4) with and without intervention. Measure zero-g offset before/after shock using calibrated reference accelerometer.
- Instruments: Shock test fixture, precision shaker, calibrated reference accelerometer, data acquisition system
- Pass/fail: Zero-g offset ≤50mg post-shock with intervention; >50mg without intervention indicates failure
- Duration: 100ms shock pulse per test
- Kill criterion: Any device showing permanent offset >50mg fails the test

- Survives 10000g shock: Verified via shock test protocol
- No permanent zero-g offset >50mg: Directly measured in test
- Uses only allowed measures: Electrostatic repulsion (not prohibited), no mechanical redesign
- No new development: Pulse generator is procurable, software update is standard practice
